commits.message:
Keep the replay source free of the follower runtime's imports

The pre-init check imported parseHubOracleOneShot from follower-runtime.ts,
which the projection determinism lint excludes as a node-reaching module, so
the replay source now reached it. The parser moves, unchanged, into its own
module that both the replay source and the deployment follower import.

projection-lints.test.ts was red on 4ef65d769 in CI (excluded_import
./follower-runtime.js from replay-source.ts) and is green here; watcher tsc,
eslint and prettier pass.
Merge the persisted, lane-serialized wallet seed

Bump the transport frame protocol to version 2

Version 2 adds noDeadline on lsq_query (the wallet seed read). A version 1
sidecar paired with a version 2 client used to pass hello and then fail
the first seed query as a terminal client_protocol_violation. With the
version bumped on both sides (TypeScript client, Go sidecar, the fake
sidecar used by tests), a mismatched pair now fails at hello with
version_unsupported, at startup. The README documents the version and why
it changed.

Test gate:
1. The transport suite fails if the built sidecar's --protocol-version is
   not 2, or if a hello at the previous version (1) is not refused with a
   fatal version_unsupported frame and exit 64. The Go session test fails
   on the same refusal at the frame layer.
2. It extends the existing version tests: the unsupported-version cases
   now send version 1 instead of an arbitrary one, so they cover the
   old-sidecar pairing this bump is for.

Red before the bump: TS 'Expected "2" Received "1"' and the version 1
hello answered malformed_frame, not version_unsupported; Go
session_test.go:222 got malformed_frame ("hello needs version, ...").

Gates run under the serial lock and run-capped, all exit 0:
- contrib native --package @al-ft/l1-node-transport (built sidecar prints
  --protocol-version 2; go vet + go test -race ok);
- contrib boundary --package @al-ft/l1-node-transport;
- contrib gate process-boundaries (21 + 77 + 22 tests passed).

Close the node connection before awaiting the follow loop on shutdown

Each role aborted the follow loop and awaited it before closing the
transport. Abort only closes the chain-sync stream, so a loop parked in a
block write behind a wallet seed read in flight (which holds the store's
writer lane and has no request deadline) never returned, and a shutdown
waited out the node's whole UTxO scan.

The watcher, the node and the committee now close the transport right
after the abort, before awaiting the loop: the read fails as at a sidecar
exit, the lane frees, and the block write and the loop finish. The
watcher's tx-input resolver closes after the loop too. The later transport
close in each release stays (it is idempotent).

Test gate:
1. The new watcher case fails if a shutdown requested while a seed read is
   in flight, with a block waiting behind it, waits for that read; it also
   fails if readiness then waits on the node, or does not name the seed
   read in flight (with its point) and the node lag as unknown.
2. It is a new file: no watcher runtime test drives a node whose ledger
   side hangs. The fake sits at the transport boundary (ledger states
   serialize as in the real transport; a closed transport fails every
   pending read). The node and committee changes have no role-level test:
   neither role has a transport seam.

Red before the fix: "expected 'still waiting' to be 'closed'" (the
shutdown still waiting 2 s after it was requested).

Never wait on the slot time in the node-behind check

The follow loop awaited slotTime after every applied event. The watcher and
the committee read the slot configuration from the node through the
transport's ledger lock, which a wallet seed read (no request deadline)
holds, so before the configuration was cached the loop parked on it and a
hung node was never reported behind.

- watchNodeBehind never awaits slotTime. A number is judged at once. A
  promise makes the lag unknown (nodeBehind { lagMs: null }), which is not
  ready ("lag behind wall-clock time unknown, waiting on the node for the
  slot configuration"), and is judged and published when it lands. A throw
  or a rejection still skips the check: the last judged result stands, and
  the next check reads again. No timer is added to the lock wait.
- The watcher and the committee answer slotTime synchronously once the slot
  configuration is read; the node already uses Lucid's synchronous clock.

Test gate:
1. The new follower case fails if the loop waits on an outstanding slot
   time (it applied 0 events within the bound) or if the outstanding read
   is reported as ready; the failure case fails if a rejected read leaves
   the lag unknown instead of the last result.
2. They extend follow-loop-node-behind.test.ts, the suite for this check;
   no case had a slot time that does not answer at once.

Red before the fix: "timed out; last status {state: starting, events: 0,
...}" for the new case. The role-level case (the watcher over a hung ledger
side, in the next commit) with this change reverted: "no seed in flight;
readiness [l1_follower_catching_up: no node tip seen yet, ...]": the loop
parked on the slot configuration after its first block.

Hold the slow seed read until the block is delivered, without a sleep

The slow-read test raced the block's write against a 300 ms sleep. The
fake ledger read now delivers the block to the store and only then answers,
so the block is always queued behind the seed when the read returns, with no
timing involved.

Test gate:
1. The test still fails if the seed's read and write do not run as one
   writer-lane task: running the store's seed outside the lane makes it
   return pending (the cursor moved under the read) instead of seeded.
2. This replaces the timing of an existing case; no new case.

Red with the seed taken out of the writer lane: "expected { kind:
'pending', ... } to match object { kind: 'seeded', ... }" on both stores.

Report a wallet seed in flight, with the point it reads at

While a seed ran, the seeder's status() still said not_initialized or the
last attempt's failure, so an operator could not tell a seed read stuck in
the node from one never started. The node's intent stage computed its seed
hold only after the step returned, and the committee kept the last step's
detail, so both showed the old reason for the whole read.

- WalletSeedPendingReason gains in_flight. While a step runs, status()
  reports it with inFlight { at, sinceMs }: at is the cursor point the
  ledger read is at, null while the seed waits for the writer lane. The
  detail reads "seed read in flight at slot S (block H) since <time>".
- seedWallets takes an optional onRead hook, called as the read starts
  inside the writer lane.
- The committee's L1 source and the node's intent stage read the seed hold
  live from status() instead of from the last step's answer.

Test gate:
1. The new tests fail if status() keeps reporting not_initialized while a
   seed read is held, if the committee's readiness or the node's holds()
   show the previous answer instead of in_flight during the read, or if the
   in-flight state outlives the step.
2. The follower case is a new file because it is a different unit (the
   seeder's status, not the seed write) and wallet-seed.test.ts is near its
   size cap; the committee and node cases extend their existing suites,
   whose fakes already reach the seed path.

Red before the fix: wallet-seeder-status.test.ts got reason
"not_initialized" where "in_flight" was expected; the committee case got
detail "own wallets not seeded yet"; the node case got [] from holds()
during the read.

Pin the replay checkpoint's persistence and a rewind that removes the init

Once the init is deep enough to be the checkpoint point, the test now
checks that the checked genesis ledger is persisted and that the replay
retention floor rises above the origin. Before that, the floor stays at
the origin. A new case rewinds the init away while the chain is still
short and expects the checkpoint to go back to pending.

Treat a replay checkpoint at or below the follower's origin as pre-init

When fewer than automaticRecoveryMaxDepth+2 blocks separate the store
origin from the protocol init, the checkpoint observation is
l1_follower_short_chain and readiness stayed
replayed_ledger_stable_observation_pending until the chain grew (up to
about 12 hours). The replay checkpoint driver now asks the follower store
whether the checkpoint point lies at or below the origin while the
recorded one-shot spend followed the origin and created the deployment's
root. Only then is it ready: nothing is advanced, persisted or released,
and every ledger replays from genesis. Any other short chain stays
pending.

The init check is shared with the confirmed-state read and now reuses the
follower's exported protocolInitIn instead of its own SQL. A test covers a
rewind landing while a pre-init checkpoint is read. The replay-source tests
are split into a fixture and a pre-init file to stay under the line limit.

Seed each own wallet once, in the writer lane, with no request deadline

The wallet seed's LSQ utxo_by_address read scans the node's whole UTxO set
(35-44 s on preprod) and failed three ways: it raced the follow loop and lost
to cursor_moved, it re-read every wallet on every restart, and the request
deadline killed it. The owner ruled out deadline tuning and Kupo; the
follower stays the only index.

- Seed once, persisted. Migration 0003_wallet_seeds adds l1_wallet_seeds
  (address, seed_slot, seed_hash; class A). A seeded wallet, one with no
  outputs included, is never read again. A committed rewind below the seed
  point deletes it with the seed rows, a reset deletes it as class A, and a
  store start deletes the point of every wallet it does not track. INV6 also
  refuses a seed point above the cursor.
- Serialized with block application. FactStore.seedWallets reads the cursor
  and the stored seed points, reads the owed wallets from the ledger and
  writes their rows and seed points as one writer-lane task, so no block,
  rewind or prune lands between the read and the write. The cursor_moved
  retry and its attempts budget are gone. The seeder keeps no retry state:
  step() is coalesced, status() gives the readiness detail, and the three
  role callers lose their own in-flight bookkeeping.
- No per-request deadline for the seed read only. LedgerStateSession.query
  takes QueryOptions { deadline: "none" }; the client skips its timer and
  sends noDeadline in the lsq_query header, and the sidecar runs that query
  with no deadline timer. Every other request keeps requestTimeoutMs. The
  request still ends with the node connection or the sidecar, so each role
  now closes the transport before the store on shutdown.

Test gate:
1. The new follower tests fail if a restart reads the ledger again for a
   seeded wallet (also one with no outputs), if a block arriving during the
   seed read moves the cursor before the write, or if a rewind's marker
   handling owes too much or too little. The transport test fails if the
   client or the sidecar abandons a no-deadline query at its deadline, or if
   the option leaks to an ordinary query.
2. They extend the existing wallet-seed and transport suites, whose fakes
   and mock node already reach these paths; no existing case covered
   persistence across a restart, a slow read under arriving blocks, or a
   query outliving requestTimeoutMs.

Red before the fix: wallet-seed.test.ts 8 failed (seeded at b3 instead of
b2; 2 queries after a restart where 1 is owed); transport.test.ts failed with
"node_timeout: the node did not answer within the request deadline". Killing
the sidecar's noDeadline branch, the rewind's marker delete or the start-time
untracked delete each turns its test red.

Move the transport's public declarations and test helpers into their own modules

transport.ts sat at 499 of the 500-line max-lines cap and its test at 486, so the no-deadline query in the next commit cannot land in either without raising the cap. This is a pure move with no behaviour change. The public option, result and error declarations (L1NodeTransportOptions, TransportUnavailableError, TransportTimeoutError, SubmitResult, MempoolSizes, LedgerStateSession: 6 declarations) move from src/transport.ts to src/transport-api.ts. The mock-node test helpers (sidecarBinary, mockNodeBinary, MAGIC, owned, mockNode, transportFor, take, expectContiguous: 8 declarations) move from tests/transport.test.ts to tests/transport-support.ts.

verify-pure-move: "Pure move confirmed: 17 top-level declarations in 1 before file(s) at 6739c8110728; 17 in 2 after file(s)" (src) and "Pure move confirmed: 13 top-level declarations in 1 before file(s) at 6739c8110728; 13 in 2 after file(s)" (tests).

Non-move edits: src/index.ts exports the moved names from ./transport-api.js; transport.ts imports them; the test helpers became exports and the test file imports them; afterEach stays in the test file. Package typecheck, lint and format-check pass; tests/transport.test.ts 15/15.

Treat a replay checkpoint below the deployment's init as the empty queue

After a fresh deployment the watcher stayed not ready with
replayed_ledger_source_pending ("replay checkpoint has no unique
confirmed-state root") until the protocol init was
automaticRecoveryMaxDepth + 2 blocks deep, about 12 hours on preprod.
The checkpoint point sits that far below the tip, and before the init
there is no root there to read.

The replay source now tells that case apart from a missing root. It
returns no ConfirmedState when, at the checkpoint point, no root and no
CorrectionLock is live, the observation admitted an empty queue, the
store's protocol-init fact (the tx spending the hub-oracle one-shot) is
strictly after the point, and that tx created the deployment's root.
The root and the CorrectionLock are minted only with the hub-oracle
token, which only the one-shot spend can mint, so a point the one-shot
outlived holds no queue. The keeper then reports ready with no head to
check: ledgers replay from genesis, and admission history stays
retained from the origin until a real checkpoint is durable.

Every other shape stays pending as before: more than one root at the
point, no root anywhere, a root from a tx that does not spend the
one-shot, the one-shot spent without creating a root or at or before
the point, a deinitialised queue, or a stray CorrectionLock.

Check the DA submitter wallet against its committee's floor before deploying

The committee refuses a submitter wallet with fewer than two plain ADA
outputs or under 80 ADA of them, but only once it starts, after the
deployment has spent. The stack's wallet step now refuses the same
wallet up front; a test pins the two numbers to the committee's own.

Give the submitting DA committee member its own availability responder wallet

The submitting member refused to start because the preprod stack never
set its availability journal or a responder key separate from its L1
submitter. Add a daResponder wallet role and write both settings into
member 0's environment, with the journal on its state volume.

Ignore the node's runtime db directory

The node's Compose files mount demo/midgard-node/db as its data
directory, and the container writes root-owned files there. Untracked and
not ignored, they were listed among the package's files, so a contrib
build in a checkout running the stack failed reading them.
